content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors extended SDM and LinBP to reparametrize a trained network with skip connections. Thus, they can employ the findings in SDM and LinBP and apply to different components. Then, the authors use a meta model, one-step attack, and an existing hyper-parameter searching algorithm to seek optimal parameters to improve transferability.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

Reparametrizing ReLU and convolution for increasing transferability can be considered novel. The comparison includes a number defense and undefended models. It also uses a large dataset with 5000 images. 


Weakness:

1.The methods selected in comparison are not comprehensive. The authors should include methods published in ICRL 2022. The methods, including I-FGSM, DI, SGM, LinBP, etc have been well suppressed by others. The authors only include two recent methods i.e., NAA and LLTA, which are published in AAAI and CVPR 2022. The selection of these methods and neglecting others published in ICRL are unclear. 

2.In the comparisons, the authors selected different methods. For example, in Table 1, NAA is not included but in right hand-side of Table 2, NAA is included. Similar situations also appears in other comparisons in the paper.

3.Only one epsilon is evaluated. 

4.No experiments on target attack.

5.The simularity of meta model and target model is a key of the proposed method. Since the proposed method has a lot of parameters, using optimization to fil the data on the meta model may "overfit" the meta model. If the meta model and target model are smilar enough, it is may not be a problem. However, if the meta model is very different from the target model, e.g., VIT and VGG, will it be a problem?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
1) Overall, the presentation quality is up to the standard. However, there are some grammatical mistakes and unclear statements.


2) The paragraph below Eq. 9 and Fig 4(a) are the worst one in the entire paper. I spent sometimes to figure out what the authors want to say. The authors use the terms significant different of attack rate |s1-s2| and significant attack difference for confidences interval of 95%. The meanings of significant different and significant attack difference are unclear. It should not be p-value and should not be alpha in the statistic test. In addition, why s1+s2=1 is the worst case? 


3) The authors consider that their method is DAG-based. My view is difference. The authors just use an optimization algorithm to search best hyper-parameters for different skip links. In fact, I feel that the abstract and the contribution are overstated.


4) Some figures can be improved, for example Fig. 1. The relationship between blocks below and the one above can draw better. 


5) I agree that reparametrizing a trained network with skip connections and using a hyper-parameter searching algorithm to search optimize parameters is novel. However, I don’t agree any contribution related to DAG.


6) For reproducibility, likely. However, some parts are unclear, paragraph below Eq. 9 and Fig 4(a)
content.summary_of_the_review:
1) Reparametrizing a trained network with skip connections and using a hyper-parameter searching algorithm to search optimize parameters is novel.

2) Evaluation is incomplete

3) Some contributions are overstated.

4) Presentation needs to be further improved.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents a method backPropagation pAth Search (PAS) to enhance adversarial transferability by searching the most transferable backpropagation path. SkipConv is proposed and leveraged when constructing the DAG-based search space, together with the existing structural reparameterization of residual and activation modules. The forward calculation of SkipConv is normal while the backpropagation includes skip connection in order to use more gradients from critical features. When searching the path, Bayesian Optimization is employed and one-step approximation is used for path evaluation to reduce the search overhead. Comprehensive experiments are conducted and the results show that PAS improves the attack success rate for many kinds of models.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:  
In this paper, adversarial transferability is handled from the backpropagation perspective and converted into an optimization problem in DAG search space, which makes it possible to find the best path with optimizable variables. 

The base experiments are comprehensive, including both normally and robustly trained models and comparing the results with existing competitive baselines. The ablation experiments are also conducted to validate the effectiveness of each part in PAS method. 

In section 3.2, the analysis of the sample size N is detailed. The relationship between N and the difference in attack success rate is visualized in Figure 4, which is helpful for understanding the idea. 

Weakness:
1. The experiment results show that the selection of surrogate models has a significant effect on attack success rate. It indicates that the used features are still related to the specific structures of surrogate models. Is there any guidance on which model should be used as a surrogate model in practice?

2. VGG19 is used as a meta model to evaluate the transferability of backpropagation paths. An ablation study on meta models should be provided. During the path search, it is not clear which model is best to be applied as a meta model for transferability evaluation. Do the multiple meta models improve the transferability further?

3. Overclaim: As the transferability is evaluated by just one model (VGG), the most transferable path is overclaimed. The found path is most transferable to the target VGG model, not all models.

4. It will be better if the authors can provide visualizations of the adversarial examples and adversarial perturbations created by the proposed methods. Do the adversarial perturbations show unique properties, compared to ones created by others?

5. Minor limitation: Limited by the backpropagation process, PAS cannot be applied to models with novel architectures (e.g. Vision Transformers) where no convolution layer is used.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Overall, the presentation is easy to follow. The proposed solution is not significantly novel but provides further techniques to improve adversarial transferability.
content.summary_of_the_review: Due to the main concern about missing important ablation studies, I tend to weak reject this work before the rebuttal.

content.summary_of_the_paper: Inspired by structural reparameterization, this paper proposes a PAS strategy to enhance the transferability of adversarial examples. The structural reparameterization strategy is based on RepVGG, which could balance the accuracy and speed. While attacking the surrogate model, the proposed dynamic backpropagation path search strategy could decide whether to skip the residual, activation, and convolution modules. According to the path search, the adversarial examples would enhance their transferability for both normal CNNs and robust CNNs. In the experiments, the authors choose 12 target models and five baselines to prove that PAS can boost the transferability of adversarial examples. Especially, the average ASSR is 16% more than the second-best attacker IAA.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
The strength of this paper is the PAS strategy could enhance the transferability of adversarial examples. The structural reparameterization strategy is based on RepVGG, which could balance the accuracy and speed. While attacking the surrogate model, the proposed dynamic backpropagation path search strategy could decide whether to skip the residual, activation, and convolution modules. According to the path search, the adversarial examples would enhance their transferability for both normal CNNs and robust CNNs. In the experiments, the authors choose 12 target models and 5 baselines to prove that PAS can boost the transferability of adversarial examples. Especially the average ASR is 16% more than the second-best attacker IAA.

The weakness of this paper is that some descriptions are unclear. First, the core of PAS is unclear. Is PAS focused on the high-sensitivity area of vanilla examples? Alternatively, the method target the weakness of surrogate models - that one path search strategy could be applied to the whole dataset. After that, in section 4.1, the authors 'conduct K = 2000', but they do not mention the definition of K. At the end of the second paragraph, the authors said, 'As PAS is inspired by RepVGG, VGG19 is used as the meta model to evaluate the transferability of backpropagation paths'. The words 'meta model' only appear twice in this paper, the author did not explain what meta model is, why they chose VGG19 as meta model, and what difference between meta model and surrogate model. In table 2 and table 3, the experiments choose several baselines(e.g., 'MI-PD,' 'FDA-MI-PD'), but they do not explain what PD attack is. And then, the experiment conducts ablation study to verify the contribution of each part. In table 4, 'w/ skipgrad' indicates that the path search strategy only has skipgrad model, which should be equal to the SGM attack. However, the ASR is not the same as the results in table 1 and table 2. They also do not mention the surrogate model in the ablation study. Finally, the RepVGG network shows favorable accuracy-speed trade-off compared to the SOTA models, but the author do not investigate the speed of PAS.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This paper is motivated by SGM and RepVGG, and the method could boost the adversarial transferability efficiently. So the novelty is enough. However, some descriptions are unclear. The authors should add more explanations on some details. They also need to improve the quality of their paper and avoid English problems. For example, on the first page, 'transfer-based attackers' could not be a 'scheme.' In the first line of the second paragraph, Goodfellow et al. 'point out' that.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper proposes to produce multiple backward paths using the idea of skip-connections on the surrogate model and searches for the most transferable one to craft adversarial examples.
For producing backward paths on general models instead of only on the common ResNet-like networks, the paper re-parameterize typical architectures. For convolution, they decompose a convolution module into an identity kernel and a residual kernel, turning the convolution operation into a residual operation that adds residuals into the original input. For the already existing skip-connection modules, the residual operation will also be preserved as a highway for backward pass. These newly added residual operations contains a scale factor $\gamma_i$ for weighting the residual adding to the original input. With different $\gamma_i$, one can acquire different backward paths to craft various adversarial examples.
As $\gamma_i$ yields infinity paths, the authors use vgg19 as a meta victim model with about 200~300 images as meta dataset to evaluate each single path. The most transferable path is selected and serves to generate adversarial examples. The adversarial examples are evaluated on natural networks, ensemble adversarial training, and defended networks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros:
1. The re-parameterized methods using distributivity of convolution let the general modules support skip-connection operations.
2. The idea of searching the gradient backward path is novel and interesting.
Cons:
1. The work does not include important techniques such as TransIation-Invariant (TI), Scale-Invariant (SI). Also, momentum (MI) can be upgraded to Nesterov Accelerated Gradient.

2. The attack method depends on an additional meta dataset of up to 200 images. There are some methods using extra images to improve transferability (Admix, TTP). Given that a certain amount of extra images is provided, it is doubtful if the improvement is enough compared to those methods.

3. The attack method uses vgg19 as the meta model for evaluating path searching. As the access to the meta model vgg19 is permitted, I recommend that there should be an ablation study about simply ensemble vgg19 with white-box surrogate models. The proposed PAS should outperform the naive ensemble.

4. The attack method needs several trials on path searching. The cost or efficiency may be concerns compared to the baseline simple iterative attacks.

5. Figure 2 may contain a misleading typo: “the normal kernel $k$ is reparameterized into the sum of the skip kernel and $I$ the residual kernel $k - I$”.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Novelty is good. The paper is also reasonably well-written. However, the experiments are not convincing enough, which decreases the overall quality.
content.summary_of_the_review: The method and idea of the paper are novel and interesting, but the baseline methods included and the experiments are not convincing enough. Also, the method's practicality is doubtful due to the dependency on an additional meta model, meta dataset, and cost on path searching.
